notes: Strong's cross-references this root to H1961 (הָיָה, "to be/become/come to pass") -- "compare H1961" -- but the two have different consonants (ה-ו-א/ה-ו-ה vs ה-י-ה) and are not a suppletion pair; noting the cross-reference for visibility, not modeling it as strong_alt.

"fall" rests on a single form, Job.37.6 (הֱוֵא אָרֶץ, "He says to the snow, 'Fall on the earth'"), a well-attested but debated translation of this hollow root applied to snow; flagging as the one form supporting that sense specifically (the other three qal forms all mean "be/become/come to pass").
